answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance-mandated security patch), and circuit breakers/read-replica routing target dependency or read-path load, not a write-path degradation. The latency is confined to the primary region during peak settlement writes, which matches the pattern in memory_b2 where regional failover restored latency within minutes. Failover also avoids data loss risk to in-flight writes if executed with proper replication checks, preserving the objective of not losing customer writes. I want to verify memory_b2 (failover mechanics and write-safety during the March event) and memory_b5 (to confirm whether read offloading contributed to write recovery, which would weaken the case for failover alone). Failover carries real risk during peak writes — replication lag could mean lost or delayed settlement writes — so the flag is raised and execution should be guarded: confirm replica lag is near zero before shifting traffic.
